literal: Without holding the sense of honor as their fence, indeed, the vast world, they will not desire, those who are noble.
translation: Noble people will not desire even the vast world if they cannot have their sense of honor as its protective fence.
modern: மேன்மையானவர்கள், நாணத்தை (தன்மானத்தை) ஒரு வேலியாகக் கொள்ளாமல், இந்த அகன்ற உலகத்தையே பெறுவதாக இருந்தாலும் அதனை விரும்ப மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of 'nan' (the sense of shame or honor) for noble individuals. Great people would not desire to possess the entire vast world if they had to do so by compromising their self-respect. The metaphor of 'nan' as a 'veli' (fence) suggests that honor is what guards and defines a person's character. Without this boundary of self-respect, even the grandest worldly achievements are worthless to the noble.
